purpose: The ways a running rust program can HOLD layer-1 content. Not layer 1 (the data is fixed), not layer 3 (no operations beyond load-and-read-back), not the type system.
reference: language knowledge, checked against ../type_vocabulary/raw/rust.types.json as a candidate checklist only (superseded node; not a decision instrument).

nothing.note: the empty tuple; a value carrying nothing.
absence spelled as a case of a two-case shape, so the hole has a declared element kind.

truth.note: two values, one byte, no numeric side.

whole.note: signed 32-bit; the narrow end of the fixed-width camp.
unsigned 64-bit; reaches u64 max, refuses anything below zero.
signed 128-bit; wide enough for every edge in the data file, still finite.

fractional.note: IEEE single; holds every base value at lower precision.

text.note: a borrowed view of utf-8 text that lives elsewhere; the literal form.
holds text only as encoded bytes; the codepoints are gone until decoded.

sequence.note: growable ordered run, one declared element kind.
fixed length written into the shape; the length is part of what it is.
a borrowed window onto a run that lives elsewhere; length known at run time.
ordered run open at both ends.
fixed length, and each position may be a different kind; the one rust sequence holder that takes the mixed row.

keyed.note: name to element, no order kept.
keyed.read: { let mut ks: Vec<String> = v.keys().cloned().collect(); ks.sort(); format!("{:?} {:?}", ks, v.len()) }

probes.emptykey: let v: HashMap<String, String> = HashMap::from([("".to_string(), "empty-string key".to_string())]);
probes.nested: let v: HashMap<String, HashMap<String, Vec<i64>>> = HashMap::from([("outer".to_string(), HashMap::from([("inner".to_string(), vec![1, 2])]))]);

keyed.note: the same grouping held in sorted key order rather than insertion order.

probes.emptykey: let v: BTreeMap<String, String> = BTreeMap::from([("".to_string(), "empty-string key".to_string())]);
probes.nested: let v: BTreeMap<String, BTreeMap<String, Vec<i64>>> = BTreeMap::from([("outer".to_string(), BTreeMap::from([("inner".to_string(), vec![1, 2])]))]);

keyed.spelling: struct R { a: i64 } R { a: 1 }
keyed.note: names fixed when the shape is written, not when the data arrives; the odd keys are not spellable as field names.

probes.flat: #[derive(Debug)] struct R3 { a: i64, b: i64, c: i64 } let v = R3 { a: 1, b: 2, c: 3 };
probes.intlike: #[derive(Debug)] struct RI { 1: i64, b: i64 } let v = RI { 1: 1, b: 2 };
probes.emptykey: #[derive(Debug)] struct RE { : String } let v = RE { : "empty-string key".to_string() };
probes.nested: #[derive(Debug)] struct RN { outer: Vec<i64> } let v = RN { outer: vec![1, 2] };

nesting.note: nesting by repeating the same holder; every level must carry the same declared kind.

probes.seq_in_map: use std::collections::BTreeMap; let v: BTreeMap<String, Vec<i64>> = BTreeMap::from([("outer".to_string(), vec![1, 2])]);
probes.mixed_depth: let v: Vec<Vec<i64>> = vec![vec![1], vec![2, 3], vec![]];

nesting.spelling: enum Node { Null, Truth(bool), Whole(i64), Text(String), Seq(Vec<Node>), Map(BTreeMap<String,Node>) }
nesting.note: a hand-written sum shape; the only rust holder that takes every layer-1 form in one element position, which is what mixed nesting needs.

probes.seq_in_seq: use std::collections::BTreeMap; #[derive(Debug)] enum Node { Null, Truth(bool), Whole(i64), Text(String), Seq(Vec<Node>), Map(BTreeMap<String, Node>) } let v = Node::Seq(vec![Node::Seq(vec![Node::Whole(1), Node::Whole(2)]), Node::Seq(vec![Node::Whole(3), Node::Whole(4)])]);
probes.seq_in_map: use std::collections::BTreeMap; #[derive(Debug)] enum Node { Null, Truth(bool), Whole(i64), Text(String), Seq(Vec<Node>), Map(BTreeMap<String, Node>) } let v = Node::Map(BTreeMap::from([("outer".to_string(), Node::Map(BTreeMap::from([("inner".to_string(), Node::Seq(vec![Node::Whole(1), Node::Whole(2)]))])))]));
probes.mixed_depth: use std::collections::BTreeMap; #[derive(Debug)] enum Node { Null, Truth(bool), Whole(i64), Text(String), Seq(Vec<Node>), Map(BTreeMap<String, Node>) } let v = Node::Seq(vec![Node::Whole(1), Node::Seq(vec![Node::Whole(2), Node::Map(BTreeMap::from([("k".to_string(), Node::Text("t".to_string()))]))]), Node::Truth(true), Node::Null]);

identity.note: the ordinary owned holder; a value can sit in only one position, so a second position needs a copy.
counted sharing with no way to change what is shared; two positions do name one object.
counted sharing plus permission to change what is shared at run time; the rust shape a shared node and a cycle both need.
